mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about sp2 hybridisation is NOT true?

options.A: It involves mixing one s orbital with two p orbitals.
options.B: The resulting three hybrid orbitals are arranged in a trigonal planar geometry.
options.C: The remaining unhybridized p orbital is perpendicular to the plane of the hybrid orbitals.
options.D: It leads to a linear molecular geometry with bond angles of 180°.

mcqs.answer: It leads to a linear molecular geometry with bond angles of 180°.
mcqs.explanation: sp2 hybridisation combines one s and two p orbitals, producing three equivalent sp2 hybrids that lie in a plane with 120° bond angles (trigonal planar). The unhybridized p orbital is perpendicular to this plane. Therefore, the statement that sp2 hybridisation gives a linear geometry of 180° is incorrect. Options A, B and C correctly describe sp2 hybridisation.

mcqs.question: Why does carbon in a methane (CH₄) molecule undergo sp³ hybridisation?

options.A: Because carbon forms four sigma bonds requiring four equivalent orbitals.
options.B: Because carbon forms a double bond with one hydrogen atom.
options.C: Because carbon needs to accommodate a lone pair of electrons.
options.D: Because carbon forms two pi bonds in the molecule.

mcqs.answer: Because carbon forms four sigma bonds requiring four equivalent orbitals.
mcqs.explanation: In methane, carbon makes four single (sigma) bonds with hydrogen. To form four equivalent sigma bonds, the 2s and three 2p orbitals mix to give four sp³ hybrid orbitals arranged tetrahedrally. Options B, C, and D describe situations that do not occur in CH₄.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a type of hybridisation with its molecular geometry and typical bond angle?
mcqs.explanation: sp³ hybridisation uses one s and three p orbitals, giving four hybrid orbitals that adopt a tetrahedral arrangement with a bond angle of about 109.5°. sp hybridisation gives a linear geometry (180°), and sp² gives trigonal planar (120°). Options A, B, and D mismatch hybridisation with geometry or angle.

mcqs.question: What is the hybridisation of the central boron atom in boron trifluoride (BF₃)?
mcqs.explanation: Boron in BF₃ forms three sigma bonds with fluorine atoms and has no lone pairs. To accommodate three equivalent sigma bonds in a planar arrangement, boron undergoes sp² hybridisation, producing three sp² hybrids at 120° angles. sp would give only two hybrids, sp³ would give four, and dsp² is used for square planar complexes, none of which apply here.

mcqs.question: In sp hybridisation, how many unhybridized p orbitals remain on the atom?
mcqs.explanation: sp hybridisation mixes one s orbital with one p orbital, producing two sp hybrid orbitals. The remaining two p orbitals stay unhybridized and are available for forming pi bonds. Hence, two unhybridized p orbitals remain.

mcqs.question: How many sigma (σ) bonds can an atom undergoing sp² hybridisation form?
mcqs.explanation: sp² hybridisation combines one s orbital with two p orbitals, yielding three sp² hybrid orbitals. Each hybrid orbital can form a sigma bond, so an sp²‑hybridised atom can form up to three σ bonds. The remaining p orbital is used for a π bond if needed.

mcqs.question: Which definition best describes sp³ hybridisation?

options.A: Mixing of one s and one p orbital to give two equivalent orbitals.
options.B: Mixing of one s and two p orbitals to give three equivalent orbitals.
options.C: Mixing of one s and three p orbitals to give four equivalent orbitals.
options.D: Mixing of one s, one p and two d orbitals to give four equivalent orbitals.

mcqs.answer: Mixing of one s and three p orbitals to give four equivalent orbitals.
mcqs.explanation: In sp³ hybridisation, the 2s orbital mixes with all three 2p orbitals, producing four sp³ hybrid orbitals that are energetically equivalent and oriented tetrahedrally. Option A describes sp, B describes sp², and D describes dsp² hybridisation used in square planar complexes.

mcqs.question: The molecule ethene (C₂H₄) has a planar geometry around each carbon atom. Which hybridisation of the carbon atoms explains this geometry?
mcqs.explanation: Each carbon in ethene forms three sigma bonds (two C–H and one C–C) and one pi bond. To accommodate three sigma bonds in a plane, the carbon atoms undergo sp² hybridisation, giving three sp² hybrids at 120° and leaving one unhybridized p orbital for the π bond. sp would give linear geometry, sp³ tetrahedral, and dsp² is not relevant here.
